[
  {"step":1,"file":"src/pcre2_fuzzsupport.c","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":55,"var":"data,size","code":"int LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(const unsigned char *data, size_t size)","note":"Attacker-controlled bytes enter the fuzz target as the raw pattern/subject corpus."},
  {"step":2,"file":"src/pcre2_fuzzsupport.c","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":82,"var":"compile_options","code":"compile_options = ((((uint32_t)r1 << 16) | ((uint32_t)r2 & 0xffff)) & ALLOWED_COMPILE_OPTIONS) | PCRE2_NEVER_BACKSLASH_C;","note":"The input-derived bytes influence compile flags; the candidate forces PCRE2_AUTO_CALLOUT so the compiled pattern emits callouts during matching."},
  {"step":3,"file":"src/pcre2_fuzzsupport.c","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":111,"var":"code","code":"code = pcre2_compile((PCRE2_SPTR)data, (PCRE2_SIZE)size, compile_options, &errorcode, &erroroffset, NULL);","note":"The attacker-controlled buffer is compiled into a regex program that may contain auto-inserted callout opcodes."},
  {"step":4,"file":"src/pcre2_fuzzsupport.c","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":166,"var":"errorcode","code":"errorcode = pcre2_match(code, (PCRE2_SPTR)data, (PCRE2_SIZE)match_size, 0, match_options, match_data, match_context);","note":"The same attacker-controlled bytes are used as the subject for matching, driving execution into the regex engine."},
  {"step":5,"file":"src/pcre2_match.c","function":"match","line":5228,"var":"rrc","code":"rrc = do_callout(F, mb, &length);","note":"When the matcher reaches an auto-callout opcode, it dispatches to the callout helper with frame state derived from the current match path."},
  {"step":6,"file":"src/pcre2_match.c","function":"do_callout","line":310,"var":"Fovector[-2],Fovector[-1]","code":"save0 = Fovector[-2]; save1 = Fovector[-1]; Fovector[-2] = Fovector[-1] = PCRE2_UNSET; rc = mb->callout(&cb, mb->callout_data);","note":"The helper writes to the two slots immediately before the working ovector before invoking the callback; the vulnerability hypothesis is that this out-of-bounds access can hit invalid memory when the frame-backed vector is not laid out as expected."}
